Because everybody who finishes asks this question. It is not a feature request. It is what happens next, structurally, to every single customer you have.

**CSM notes, Karin Wallin, 2026-08-20:**

Aalborg Food Group. 40,000 ARR, largest logo we have lost, notice given 11 June, term ends 11 September, already live on Verdanta. Churn reason field says Competitor. That is true and it is not the reason.

Not price. Verdanta is roughly 15% more expensive than we were and price was not mentioned in their decision meeting.

Not delivery. Fourteen brands across two systems live in five months, auditor accepted with three questions against forty the previous year under a consultant. She volunteered all of this unprompted and asked me to make sure it was recorded.

The reason is that they finished. She had the number in February, took it to the board and the fund, and somebody asked what they were going to do about it. She came back to Petra and got an honest answer about scenario comparison versus costed pathways, and then four instances of "on the roadmap" across four months, which she had written down and counted.

**The thing I need to take to product, and it is not the feature request.** She says the fund wanted a directional planning artefact, low medium high cost bands, nothing auditable, nothing anybody would hold them to. We refused to give her a soft number to protect a standard of rigour that was hers to waive and not ours. Her words: the rigour you were protecting was my rigour, not yours, and you made that decision on my behalf for four months without asking me. Verdanta gave her the soft version and told her it was soft.

Second, smaller, and still real. Nine brand manager licences, four logins in nine months. She was the interface. Every number that reached anybody who could act on it went via her and a screenshot. Six of nine have logged into Verdanta in eight weeks, and she does not think their product is better, she thinks they have a page that shows a brand manager his brand and nothing else.

Jesper Find, group reporting, joined for fifteen minutes and gave us the counter evidence. Our change log saved them six weeks at audit, Verdanta's is thinner and he has already argued with it, and he raised this in the decision meeting and lost. His framing: an annual benefit to a function of two against a quarterly question to the board. He also told Tobias in the autumn that he could not give single entity read access without exposing the whole navigation, and he believes Tobias raised it, and he is right that this is the problem rather than the excuse.

Nobody from product has ever spoken to this account. Eleven months, one of our three largest the whole time, Petra and Tobias only.

Her closing advice, which I think is the most valuable thing in the recording: stop counting customers who request reduction planning and start counting customers who have finished their first measurement cycle, because every one of them arrives at this question. It is not a feature request, it is what structurally happens next to every customer we have.

Petra flagged this risk in March. Three months between the flag and the notice, six months between the board question and this call, and nothing changed in any of them. That is the finding for me and it is not about a module.
